ra: Rashnu the Just is the yazata who weighs souls' deeds at the Chinvat Bridge (Vendidad 19).
Rashnu presides over the judgement of the soul at the Chinvat Bridge (was 'judges'; corrected to presides_over since judges takes a being/Dead object in house convention).
Mithra is one of the three judging yazatas at the Chinvat Bridge in Zoroastrian eschatology.
Sraosha conducts and protects the soul on its passage across the bridge (was 'guides'; corrected since guides takes a being/Dead object).
The Daena, the personified conscience, meets the soul at the Chinvat Bridge and leads the righteous onward.
Garothman, the House of Song, is the abode of Ahura Mazda and the blessed.
Drujo Demana, the House of Lies, is the abode of Angra Mainyu and the damned.
The House of Lies is the structural antithesis of the House of Song in Zoroastrian eschatology.
The righteous soul reaches Garothman by crossing the Chinvat Bridge.
The wicked soul falls from the Chinvat Bridge into the House of Lies.
Hamistagan is the neutral middle state distinct from both paradise (Garothman) and hell.
Souls in Hamistagan await release at the final renovation brought by the Saoshyant (Frashokereti).
Ereshkigal is queen of Irkalla/Kur, the Mesopotamian netherworld (Descent of Ishtar).
Ereshkigal rules the land of no return.
Nergal becomes consort and co-ruler of the netherworld with Ereshkigal.
Ganzir is the gate/threshold belonging to the netherworld Irkalla (was 'part_of', which is not a valid relationship_type; belongs_to_realm is attested for place-within-realm).
Ishtar descends into Irkalla and is detained there in the Descent of Ishtar.
Enki provides fresh water to Dilmun in the myth Enki and Ninhursag, making it the pure land.
Dilmun, the deathless pure land, stands in mythic contrast to the netherworld of death.
The seven hekhalot are situated within Araboth, the seventh of the seven heavens.
The seven palaces are contained within the highest heaven of the sevenfold cosmos (was 'part_of', invalid; belongs_to_realm is the attested place-within-realm type).
Angelic gatekeepers of the Heavenly Host guard the entrances to each of the seven palaces in Hekhalot Rabbati.
Metatron, the heavenly prince/scribe, presides over the upper palaces and the Throne in Merkavah literature.
Araboth, the seventh heaven, houses the Throne of Glory.
The rabbinic/Merkavah seven heavens parallel but are distinct from the seven firmaments of Sefer ha-Razim.
Both are vertical hierarchies of the Jewish-mystical cosmos; the four Kabbalistic worlds are a later systematization overlapping the heavens schema.
The ascending heavens stand opposite Gehenna, the lower realm of punishment, in Jewish cosmology.
